chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man trims his nails, cuts his moustache, and takes from the hair of his head and his beard—does that invalidate his wudu (ablution)?

So he said: O Zurarah, all of this is sunnah (prophetic tradition), while wudu (ablution) is an obligation, and nothing from the sunnah invalidates the obligation; rather, that indeed increases him in purification.

key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a prophetic practice, recommended norm, or established tradition

ai.seo_question: Does cutting nails, trimming the moustache, or cutting hair break wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that trimming the nails, cutting the moustache, and taking hair from the head or beard do not invalidate wudu (ablution). Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام distinguishes between sunnah (recommended prophetic practice) and an obligatory state, clarifying that such acts of grooming only add to cleanliness and purification.
